title: Diagonalizable matrices via squarefree minimal polynomial

problemStatement.formal: \text{For } A \in \mathrm{M}_n(K)\text{ over a field } K\text{: } A \text{ is diagonalizable } \iff \mathrm{Squarefree}(\mathrm{minpoly}_K A) \land (\mathrm{minpoly}_K A) \text{ splits over } K.
problemStatement.plain: Characterize matrix diagonalizability via the minimal polynomial: a matrix is diagonalizable over a field K iff its minimal polynomial is squarefree AND splits over K. Over algebraically closed fields, the splitting clause is vacuous; over perfect non-algebraically-closed fields (e.g. R, Q) both conditions are needed.

insights: Endomorphism-level biconditional ALREADY in-tree: CayleyHamiltonMinpolyOQ01.lean:206-211 proves f.IsSemisimple iff Squarefree (minpoly K f) for f : Module.End K V with [FiniteDimensional K V], via Mathlib's IsSemisimple.minpoly_squarefree (forward) and isSemisimple_of_squarefree_aeval_eq_zero (reverse). OQ-02 inherits this and adds only matrix-level packaging.

Splitting hypothesis is load-bearing outside IsAlgClosed: the R-rotation matrix [[0,-1],[1,0]] has minpoly X^2+1, which is squarefree (irreducible over R) but not split over R; the matrix is not diagonalizable over R (eigenvalues ±i ∉ R). Hence the correct universal characterization has TWO clauses: Squarefree AND Splits. Over IsAlgClosed K every polynomial splits, so the splitting clause is vacuous and the bare squarefree criterion suffices.

Question's 'perfect field' phrasing conflates two distinct concepts: (a) every perfect field is the setting where IsSemisimple(f) iff Squarefree(minpoly f) — this holds; (b) diagonalizability further requires splitting — this is NOT automatic outside IsAlgClosed even for perfect fields. The original problem statement appears to conflate 'perfect' with 'algebraically closed'.

Mathlib v4.26.0 has Module.End.IsSemisimple as the field-agnostic abstraction, with both directions of the squarefree biconditional packaged. Whether a parallel Module.End.IsDiagonalisable predicate exists with the same name is unconfirmed at S1; if absent, OQ-02-OQ-02 will need a local fallback definition (~50 lines).

OQ-02 has the shortest roadmap of the three parent open questions: ~420 lines vs ~930 for OQ-01 (JNF, needs nilpotent canonical form sub-OQ at ~400 lines) vs ~900 for OQ-03 (RCF, needs invariant-factor decomposition via Module.equiv_directSum_of_isTorsion). The reason: no Jordan-block / Smith-normal-form / nilpotent-shift-basis infrastructure needed; only the matrix-to-endomorphism translation layer plus the splitting-to-eigenbasis spectral step.

The splitting-to-eigenbasis implication routes through Mathlib's spectral theory in Mathlib.LinearAlgebra.Eigenspace.* but is not packaged as a single named lemma. Squarefree minpoly that splits = product of distinct (X - μᵢ); the eigenspaces ker(f - μᵢ•id) are independent (distinct eigenvalues) and their sum is the whole space (CRT on K[X]/(minpoly)). Concatenating bases of eigenspaces gives the eigenbasis. ~50 lines of plumbing.

OQ-02 is the best candidate for a single-PR S2 deliverable among the three parent OQs: scaffold + S2-OQ-01 (Matrix.IsDiagonalizable definition + API + main theorem statement with sorry) fits in ~120-150 lines following the OQ-01 / OQ-03 S1 scaffold template established in MinpolyCharpolyOQ01.lean / MinpolyCharpolyOQ03.lean.

Aristotle suitability per sub-OQ: OQ-02-OQ-01 (definitional unfolds + IsUnit manipulation) and OQ-02-OQ-04 (one-line IsAlgClosed.splits collapse) are reasonable Aristotle targets; OQ-02-OQ-02 (matrix-endomorphism bridge via Matrix.toLin') is partially Aristotle-suitable depending on lemma granularity; OQ-02-OQ-03 (splitting-to-eigenbasis spectral step) is NOT Aristotle-suitable as it routes through advanced Mathlib spectral theory.
